# OMERO Annotate.AI [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/omero-annotate-ai)](https://pypi.org/project/omero-annotate-ai/) [![install with bioconda](https://img.shields.io/badge/install%20with-bioconda-brightgreen.svg?style=flat)](http://bioconda.github.io/recipes/omero-annotate-ai/README.html) [![Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/omero-annotate-ai)](https://pypi.org/project/omero-annotate-ai/) [![CI/CD](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai/actions) [![Documentation](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/) [![Pixi Badge](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prefix-dev/pixi/main/assets/badge/v0.json)](https://pixi.sh) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai)](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai/blob/main/LICENSE) **Reproducible AI-assisted annotation of OMERO data, from image selection to training-ready datasets.** Pick images from an OMERO project, dataset, plate or screen. Annotate them in napari with [micro-SAM](https://github.com/computational-cell-analytics/micro-sam) or prepare them for [Cellpose](https://www.cellpose.org). The masks, ROIs and a tracking table go back to OMERO. Every run is described by one YAML file, so you can resume it, repeat it or share it.
![micro-SAM segmentation of a Cell Painting field in napari](docs/images/napari_microsam.jpg) micro-SAM (`vit_b_lm`) instance segmentation of nuclei in a Cell Painting field from the BioImage Archive (S-BIAD855), shown in napari. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR A[OMERO
project · dataset · plate · screen] --> B[Select images
train / val / test split] B --> C[Annotate in napari
micro-SAM or Cellpose] C --> D[Back to OMERO
masks · ROIs · tracking table] D --> E[Training data
micro-SAM · BiaPy · DL4MicEverywhere] D --> F[BioImage Archive
MIFA export] ``` - **Jupyter widgets** to connect to OMERO and create a training set or open one to continue, no code needed. - **Resumable and crash-safe:** each mask is saved locally, uploaded with a tag and then recorded in the tracking table, so an interrupted run continues where it stopped without duplicate uploads; pixel digests flag files that changed afterwards. - **Review and correct** earlier annotations with their saved masks; record a note per session. - **Flexible sampling:** timepoints, z-slices, 3D volumes, random patches, and filtering plate wells on their key-value pairs. - **Training-ready output:** one folder layout for micro-SAM, BiaPy and DL4MicEverywhere, with images and labels paired by name. - **FAIR by default:** the config carries study and method metadata and exports to the BioImage Archive (MIFA). - **Local-only storage** (`storage: local`) for data you cannot write to, such as public [IDR](https://idr.openmicroscopy.org) OME-Zarr. ## Jupyter widgets
Connect to any OMERO server. Choose a project, dataset, plate or screen.
## napari plugin (experimental) Annotate in your own napari window: **Plugins → OMERO Annotate AI → Annotate training set** (install with `pip install "omero-annotate-ai[napari]"`). It opens existing training sets on OMERO or in a local folder, saves each accepted image straight away, and can review annotated images starting from their saved masks. See the [napari plugin guide](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/napari-plugin/). ## Installation ```bash # Recommended: pixi pixi init myproject && cd myproject pixi add micro_sam jupyterlab pixi add --pypi "omero-annotate-ai[notebooks]" # Or: conda + pip conda install -c conda-forge micro_sam jupyterlab pip install "omero-annotate-ai[notebooks]" # Or: pip only (micro-SAM and napari from PyPI) pip install "omero-annotate-ai[microsam,notebooks]" jupyterlab ``` See the [installation guide](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/installation/) for details and troubleshooting. ## Quick start **With widgets** (in Jupyter): ```python from omero_annotate_ai import create_omero_connection_widget, create_workflow_widget conn_widget = create_omero_connection_widget() conn_widget.display() conn = conn_widget.get_connection() workflow_widget = create_workflow_widget(connection=conn) workflow_widget.display() # New training set, or Open one to continue ts = workflow_widget.training_set() workflow_widget.annotate(note="nuclei only, small debris skipped") ``` **From a YAML config** (scripts, batch runs, or repeating a run): ```python from omero_annotate_ai import TrainingSet, load_config config = load_config("annotation_config.yaml") ts = TrainingSet.create(config, conn) ts.annotate() ``` **Continue later** (after closing napari, or a crash): open the set by its table ID and annotate what is left; anything a crash left half-done is repaired first. ```python ts = TrainingSet.open(12345, conn) ts.extend(train_n=10) # optional: add images to the same table ts.annotate(note="second round") ``` Each training set keeps its files in one folder: images, masks, `config.yaml` (with the sessions and their notes) and a local copy of the tracking table. By default that is `~/omero_annotate_ai//_/`; set `OMERO_ANNOTATE_AI_HOME` (or pass `home=` to `TrainingSet.create` / `open`) to keep the sets elsewhere. `ts.review()` reopens annotated images with their masks to correct them. Open the same set on another computer to carry on there; two people can even annotate it at the same time, because each session claims the images it shows (your own claims, e.g. after a dropped connection, never block you). `create_pipeline(config, conn).run_full_micro_sam_workflow()` from 0.4 still works but is deprecated. The [configuration guide](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/configuration/) lists every option. ## Example notebooks | | Jupyter | marimo | |---|---|---| | Annotate with micro-SAM or Cellpose | [widget workflow](notebooks/jupyter/annotation/omero-annotate-ai-annotation-widget.ipynb) | [annotation](notebooks/marimo/omero-annotate-ai-annotation.py) | | Run from YAML (OMERO or OME-Zarr) | | [from YAML](notebooks/marimo/annotate-from-yaml.py) | | Train micro-SAM | | [micro-SAM](notebooks/marimo/omero-training-microsam.py) | | Export for BiaPy / DL4MicEverywhere | [export](notebooks/jupyter/training/omero-training-export.ipynb) | | | Export to the BioImage Archive | [BIA export](notebooks/jupyter/export_annotations/omero-table-to-bioimage-archive.ipynb) | | | Try it on public data | | [IDR OME-Zarr demo](notebooks/marimo/idr-zarr-demo.py) | ## Documentation Upgrading from 0.4? The [release notes](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/release-notes/) list the changes and how to migrate. Full documentation: **https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/** ([micro-SAM tutorial](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/tutorials/microsam-annotation-pipeline/), [API reference](https://leiden-cell-observatory.github.io/omero_annotate_ai/api/)). ## Contributing ```bash git clone https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai.git cd omero_annotate_ai pixi install # default env: everything to run the notebooks pixi run -e dev install-hooks # once per clone: ruff + notebook-output hooks pixi run -e dev pytest tests/ # dev env adds test, lint and type-check tools ``` Issues and pull requests are welcome on [GitHub](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory/omero_annotate_ai/issues). ## Contact and acknowledgements **Maarten Paul**, m.w.paul@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl Developed at the [Leiden Cell Observatory](https://github.com/Leiden-Cell-Observatory) within the [NL-BioImaging](https://github.com/NL-BioImaging) infrastructure, funded by NWO. ## License GNU General Public License v2.0 or later (GPL-2.0-or-later); see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The package builds on [omero-py](https://github.com/ome/omero-py) (GPL-2.0-or-later) and [ezomero](https://github.com/TheJacksonLaboratory/ezomero) (GPL-2.0), so it uses a compatible license. Releases up to and including 0.4.x were published under Apache-2.0.
